title: Job body sandbox has no Intl, so a job that needs time-zone date maths cannot migrate from the deprecated handler key to body
body:
Found by objectstack-ai/duly#147 on @objectstack 18.2.0 (measured on duly `main` `3834578`).

## What happens

The spec marks a job's `handler` key DEPRECATED in favour of `body`. duly's dispatch job cannot make that move. Inside the job `body` sandbox (QuickJS), `typeof Intl === 'undefined'`, and `ctx` carries only `object`, `recordId`, `api`, `log`, `crypto` and `title`.

The dispatcher computes each duty's current period in that duty's own IANA time zone, which needs `Intl.DateTimeFormat` with a `timeZone` option. Without `Intl`, or a platform date helper on `ctx` that takes a time zone, `body` cannot express the job. So the app keeps `handler`.

On 18.2.0 the deprecation no longer prints an author-time warning, so nothing tells the author about the dead end until the key is removed.

## What would unblock it

One of these:

- expose `Intl` (at least `DateTimeFormat` with `timeZone`) in the job `body` sandbox, or
- give `ctx` a date helper that resolves a calendar date and period boundaries in a named IANA zone.

Then document which one it is in the `handler` → `body` migration message.

Until then, `handler` should not be removed while a job's maths depends on time zones.
